item.title: Theater League of Clifton Announces Auditions for “1776” — Wed Sep 23, 7:00 PM — NJ
item.description: The Theater League of Clifton will hold auditions for its upcoming production of “1776” on Tuesday, September 15; Wednesday, September 16; and Thursday, September 17, from 7:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. Callbacks by invitation may also be held Thursday, September 17. Auditions will be held at Living Hope, 303 Maplewood Ave., Clifton, NJ 07013. Performances will be held November 13, 14 and 15 at the Wayne Community Center, 1 Pike Drive, Wayne, NJ. The production will be directed by Maren Sugarman. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 dramatizes the struggle within the Second Continental Congress to declare American independence. John Adams, Benjamin Franklin and Thomas Jefferson attempt to persuade a divided Congress to break with England while political, regional and personal conflicts threaten to derail the effort. item.title: Watchung Booksellers Hosts Rebecca Blumenstein and Diana Kapp, Authors of The Last Free Women — Wed Sep 23, 7:00 PM — Watchung Booksellers Kids Room
item.description:
Watchung Booksellers welcomes Rebecca Blumenstein and Diana Kapp, authors of The Last Free Women: A Daring Escape from Afghanistan and Coming of Age in America on Wednesday, September 23 at 7:00 p.m. From Rebecca Blumenstein, President, Editorial of NBC News, and journalist Diana Kapp, The Last Free Women is the extraordinary account of The New York Times’s effort to save hundreds of lives during the 2021 Afghanistan evacuation, highlighting four exceptional young women who, having escaped the fate of their fellow countrywomen back home, now face the challenges of forging a new life in a new land, a new language, and a new culture. Tickets are $5 and include a 10% discount on the book purchased at the event. To register, visit watchungbooksellers.com. Share this: Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook

item.title: Leyla McCalla in Concert — Thu Sep 24, 7:30 PM — first congregation church
item.description:
Born in New York City to Haitian emigrants and activists, Leyla McCalla finds inspiration from her past and present– her music vibrates with three centuries of history and influences from around the globe. McCalla possesses a stunning mastery of the cello, tenor banjo and guitar and, as a multilingual singer and songwriter, has risen to produce a distinctive sound that reflects the union of her roots and experience. In addition to her solo work, McCalla is a founding member of Our Native Daughters (with Rhiannon Giddens, Amythyst Kiah and Allison Russell) and alumna of Grammy award-winning Black string band The Carolina Chocolate Drops.
